sentences.text: Bicharracosaurus is estimated to have reached about 15 meters in length and to have weighed roughly 20 tonnes.
The middle and rear tail vertebrae display a triangular pneumatic opening within the centrodiapophyseal fossa, a cavity that would have been filled with air sacs.
Near the base of the neck, the last few vertebrae bear a small upward-pointing bump on the lower edge of the postzygodiapophyseal lamina, a subtle bony projection.
The sacral vertebrae, which connect the spine to the pelvis, have boat-shaped joint surfaces on their centra, indicating a distinctive articulation.
The type specimen of Bicharracosaurus was uncovered in Argentina’s Chubut Province, close to the Chubut River.
Local farmer Dionide Mesa reported the find in March 2001.
The generic name combines the Spanish term for “big animal” with the Greek word for “lizard”.
The specific epithet dionidei honors the farmer who discovered the fossil.
Bicharracosaurus is placed within Macronaria, a major clade of sauropod dinosaurs, and may be closely related to brachiosaurids.
The animal lived in the Late Jurassic, specifically from the Oxfordian to the Kimmeridgian stages.
This time interval spans roughly 161.5 to 149.2 million years ago.
Its remains have been recovered from the Cañadón Calcáreo Formation of Argentina.
Analyses have tested the phylogenetic position of Bicharracosaurus using datasets that include both basal eusauropods and neosauropods.
Researchers disagree over whether it is closely related to the contemporaneous Tehuelchesaurus benitezii, as different studies produce conflicting results.
The early evolution of macronarians remains uncertain because related taxa shift positions depending on the dataset employed.
